skipSemantics: May-skip, not must-skip: a listed test that runs and passes on a machine where its precondition holds is green. Matching is exact on the pre-'(' portion of the TRX result testName (xunit theory rows serialize with arguments, e.g. Class.Method(x: 1)); a name with no parens matches whole. Anchor is the TRX result list, never Counters arithmetic.
admissionRule: allowedSkips is not a quarantine list. A test may be listed only when its precondition is a property of the machine or OS that cannot be satisfied by configuration during a contract run, and its change names the machine class where it executes. Two named PERMANENT BANS apply: (1) CcpClient.Tests.DataRootOverrideTests.DefaultSettingsPath_EnvUnset_IsThePlatformDefault must never be allowed to skip because a process-wide CCP_DATA_ROOT override makes the floor vacuous; (2) CcpClient.Tests.ChaosTunnelLoopbackTests.Logging_RouteClassesOnly_NeverFilenameOrQuery must be fixed at the source, never quarantined.
bumpRule: Bump total only in the same commit as the test change that moves the count, with the reason recorded here. Never widen, disable, or special-case a check to make a step pass. Adding a name to allowedSkips requires the admission rule above and the machine class where it executes.
lastMovedBy: Merged the path-portability lane: +3 unit, 0 headless. ONE ROOT CAUSE behind both defects the first Linux run found: System.IO.Path answers with the HOST's rules, and a path that arrived from somewhere else - a Windows-authored session document, a synced preset, a name a hosted page typed - does not follow them. GetFileName of a Windows-style path returns the WHOLE STRING on Linux, because a backslash is an ordinary filename character there; and GetInvalidFileNameChars is 2 characters on Linux against Windows' 41. New PortablePath.FileName/InvalidFileNameChars; five product sites fixed - the two confirmed defects plus three the sweep found, including a user-facing 'Drawing ...' notice whose own doc comment already promised it printed the FILE NAME only and which printed the whole path on Linux. THE BEHAVIOUR FACTS CANNOT INVERT ON WINDOWS, and that is the shape of this entire class: on Windows both separators ARE separators and the invalid set IS the 41-char one, which is exactly why it survived until a Linux machine ran the suite. So the Windows-side inversion is carried by a SOURCE GUARD (PathPortabilityGuardTests) that fails on the un-fixed tree, banning GetInvalidFileNameChars and drive-letter literals under client/src with ZERO suppressions, because there are zero legitimate hits. A blanket ban on literal-backslash path handling was deliberately NOT built: it would fire on five CORRECT sites (URL traversal guards, manifest normalisation, Linux /proc/mounts un-escaping) and the waiver list would BE the guard. CcpClient.Tests 2697 to 2700, CcpClient.HeadlessTests unchanged at 155.
